summary:
Space Benders is an interactive, browser-based cooperative space mission design game that transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into an engaging, hands-on learning experience. Designed for 1–4 players, the game challenges participants to collaborate as engineering teams, assemble spacecraft, manage limited resources, and prepare missions to destinations across the Solar System.

Players explore six progressively challenging missions, from Low Earth Orbit to Titan, using a catalogue of 84 spacecraft components. Every engineering decision involves real trade-offs affecting mass, power, fuel, communications, radiation protection, scientific capabilities, and budget. A 12-rule engineering validation system evaluates each spacecraft, explains failures, and encourages players to improve their designs through experimentation.

The game also features real-time multiplayer collaboration and an AI-powered Flight Director that guides players through engineering challenges and provides mission recommendations.

By grounding gameplay in NASA science, real spacecraft technologies, and planetary environments, Space Benders bridges the gap between theoretical space education and practical engineering thinking. It makes space mission design accessible, encourages teamwork and critical thinking, and inspires the next generation of space engineers.
details:
Space Benders is a cooperative, browser-based space mission design game that allows 1–4 players to experience the challenges of real spacecraft engineering. Players work together as specialized engineering teams to design, assemble, and validate spacecraft capable of completing missions across the Solar System.

The game begins with players joining a crew and selecting engineering roles: Power & Thermal, Structure & Computing, Communications, and Science. They then choose from six progressively challenging missions, ranging from Low Earth Orbit and the Moon to Mars, Europa, the Sun, and Titan.

Inside an interactive virtual cleanroom, players physically collect and install components from a catalogue of 84 engineering parts. Each component affects multiple spacecraft parameters, including mass, power consumption, fuel requirements, heat protection, radiation shielding, communications, scientific output, and budget. This creates interconnected engineering trade-offs where improving one system can introduce new constraints in another.

Once the spacecraft is assembled, players run a 12-rule launch validation system that checks whether their design satisfies the mission requirements. Each rule provides pass/fail feedback, actual values, required thresholds, and explanations. Teams can modify their spacecraft, experiment with alternative configurations, and repeat the evaluation until all requirements are satisfied.

The game also integrates Google Gemini as an AI Flight Director, offering interactive engineering guidance, mission evaluations, and recommendations through dedicated tools. Engineering calculations remain deterministic and are handled by the game's validation engine.

From a technical perspective, Space Benders was developed using TypeScript, Phaser 3, Vite, Node.js, Express 5, and Colyseus for real-time multiplayer communication. Custom WebGL and WebGL2 shaders power the interactive Earth background and hyperspace launch sequence. SVG is used for the campaign map, while Google Gemini provides the AI assistance.

The project's creativity lies in combining cooperative gameplay, physical component transportation, realistic engineering constraints, and AI-assisted problem-solving into one educational experience. Unlike conventional educational games that simply present information, Space Benders allows players to learn through experimentation, collaboration, and failure.

During development, our team considered scientific accuracy, engineering trade-offs, accessibility for young learners, multiplayer coordination, gameplay performance, and educational value. Mission environments, planetary conditions, and spacecraft technologies were grounded in NASA science and real mission references.

Our intended impact is to make complex space engineering concepts accessible to students, encourage teamwork and critical thinking, and inspire young learners to explore aerospace engineering and space science through an engaging, interactive experience.
